prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1060; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed collision in a retail parking lot. Insured reports the other vehicle backed into the driver's side door while the insured was stopped in a marked space. Police report not filed on scene; property damage only at first notice. Claimant reported at first contact that they were not injured. Photos requested from insured and received.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the insured. Insured confirms both vehicles were moving at very low speed and no airbag deployment occurred. Claimant later reported headache and dizziness and sought medical evaluation. Medical records requested with authorization. Coverage confirmed under liability policy for the at-fault party's carrier; this file handled as third-party bodily injury.

Entry 3: Claimant is now represented by counsel. All further contact to go through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and logged. Attorney requested the complete claim file and the at-fault driver's policy limits. Limits disclosure request forwarded to supervisor for handling under company guidelines.

Entry 4: Medical records received from the treating clinic. Diagnosis documented as concussion with post-concussive symptoms. Treating physician recommends follow-up with neurology and a period of restricted activity. Attorney's demand package expected within thirty days. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the reported injury severity.

Entry 5: Independent medical examination scheduled through counsel's office. Adjuster reviewed the vehicle appraisal, which supports the reported impact pattern. Liability for the collision appears clear based on the statements and photos. File remains open pending receipt of the demand, IME results, and updated treatment records.
